tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: List all folders in the connected mailbox.

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Search a folder. criteria examples: ALL, UNSEEN, FROM alice@example.com.

tools.name: read_message
tools.description: Read one message by IMAP UID.

tools.name: flag_message
tools.description:
Flag a message. action: seen, unseen, flagged, unflagged, deleted.

        deleted moves the message to the mailbox's Trash folder (recoverable). Use empty_trash to delete permanently.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send email via SMTP. Pass confirm=true to actually send. Otherwise returns a preview.

tools.name: empty_trash
tools.description: Permanently delete every message in the Trash folder. Returns a preview (folder and message count) unless confirm=true.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "send_email" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_messages, read_message · Public sink: send_email · Destructive: flag_message, empty_trash.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_messages, read_message · Public sink: send_email · Destructive: flag_message, empty_trash

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
